paragraphs.source_en: = ~(-2 - degree of homogeneity in 2"). We can decompose a wave function into eigenstates of s. These are then precisely the wave functions of definite homogeneity. For example, a spinless particle with zero helicity has a twistor wave function of homogeneity -2. A left-handed spin-! particle has helicity s = - ~ and therefore has a twistor wave function with homogeneity -1, whereas a right-handed version of such a particle (helicity s = 9) would have a twistor wave function of homogeneity -3. For spin 2, the right- and left-handed twistor wave functions have respective homogeneities -6 and +2. This may look a little lopsided, as after all GR is left-right symmetric. But this may not be such a bad thing, as Nature herself is left-right asymmetric. Furthermore, the Ashtekar "new variables," which are very powerful tools in GR, are also left-right asymmetric.
